title: Theoretical Foundations
description: Focuses on the philosophical debates, moral dilemmas, and logical deductions.

subtags.description: Prioritization and balance between Dharma (duty), Artha (wealth), and Kāma (desire), and how individuals navigate conflicts between them.
examples: Choosing duty over pleasure in a moral dilemma
Pursuing wealth without violating ethical principles
Balancing sensual enjoyment with social responsibility

subtags.description: Debate between reliance on scriptural authority versus personal experience, observation, or practical knowledge.
examples: Following prescribed rules versus adapting to real-life situations
Commentarial justification based on earlier texts
Conflict between lived experience and scriptural injunctions

subtags.description: Counter-arguments against religious or ethical systems, emphasizing material reality, skepticism, and practical enjoyment.
examples: Arguments denying afterlife or karmic consequences
Prioritizing pleasure over duty
Criticism of ritual and scriptural authority

subtags.description: The purpose of human actions, encompassing Dharma, Artha, Kāma, and sometimes Mokṣa, as guiding principles of life.
examples: Understanding life as pursuit of multiple goals
Integration of pleasure within a broader ethical life
Debates on the supremacy of one goal over others

subtags.description: Debate between destiny (fate, divine will) and personal effort, and how outcomes are shaped by each.
examples: Success attributed to effort versus luck
Debate on whether love is predetermined or cultivated
Justification of actions through fate

subtags.description: Analogies, reasoning patterns, and logical proofs used by commentators to justify interpretations and arguments.
examples: Use of analogy to explain emotional behavior
Logical justification for social norms
Inference used to support unseen motivations

subtags.description: Moral failings and remedies, including recognition of wrongdoing and prescribed methods of atonement.
examples: Adultery followed by prescribed penance
Breaking social norms and seeking purification
Internal guilt and external restitution

subtags.description: What one must do according to role, context, and ethical expectations, even when it conflicts with personal desire.
examples: Fulfilling marital duties despite personal conflict
Acting according to societal expectations
Choosing obligation over pleasure

subtags.description: Situations where lying or breaking rules is justified due to higher ethical or practical considerations.
examples: Deceiving to protect a relationship
Breaking a rule to avoid greater harm
Strategic lying in romantic or social contexts

subtags.description: Abstinence and self-control, including restraint of senses and disciplined conduct in pursuit of higher goals.
examples: Practicing celibacy during student life
Resisting temptation for long-term benefit
Balancing restraint with engagement in worldly life
